summary.text: A 10-year-old girl presented with a 2-year history of an asymptomatic lesion on her back, growing over the last 2 months. Examination showed a pinkish-reddish nodule on the right back, 1 cm in diameter, and she had no significant past medical history.

Contact non-polarized dermoscopy showed a non-specific homogeneous pattern, and polarized dermoscopy showed polymorphic central vessels with whitish areas on an erythematous structureless background. Histopathology showed a nodular dermal proliferation of epithelioid cells in dense collagenous stroma, with mild to moderate atypia and occasional mitotic figures, without higher-grade cytonuclear atypia or perineural invasion. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD10, MiTF, NSE, vimentin and SMA and negative for fifteen other markers; a diagnosis of cellular neurothekeoma was made based on the immunophenotypic profile and morphological features.
The lesion was removed with 3 mm of surgical margins. After 1 year of follow-up, no local recurrence was observed.
